kurz: Soak dried beans and chickpeas overnight in salted water: they cook faster, more evenly and burst less.
bild_im_kopf: Like raisins in rum: they plump up before the real work begins.
was_passiert: During soaking the dried seeds take up roughly their own weight in water. Salt in the water swaps out calcium in the skin, which softens it. Some of the hard-to-digest sugars pass into the water.
warum_wichtig: Unsoaked beans turn soft on the outside but stay hard inside, and the skins split.
faustregeln: Hard water? Add a pinch of [[natron|baking soda]] to the soaking water.
schritte: Pick over the pulses and rinse them.
Soak in three times their volume of water with about 1 tsp salt per litre, for 8–12 hours (as a guide).
Pour off the soaking water and cook until soft in fresh water.
Lentils and split peas need no soaking.

mythos.richtig: Not true. Salt in the soaking water actually softens the skin. What keeps them hard is acid and calcium.
